summary:
IGNIS (Intelligent Guidance & NASA Insights System) is an interactive scientific exploration platform developed to make combustion and fire behaviour in microgravity easier to understand. It brings together NASA-related research resources, an interactive data laboratory, a combustion comparison studio, scientific visualizations, and an AI-powered research assistant.

The platform allows users to explore space-combustion investigations, upload and analyse CSV datasets, compare documented research parameters, visualize scientific concepts, and ask questions about combustion science.

IGNIS addresses the challenge by transforming complex research information into an accessible, interactive experience. It helps users explore how combustion behaves differently in microgravity compared with Earth and understand why these differences matter for spacecraft fire-safety research and future human spaceflight.

By connecting scientific research with interactive technology, IGNIS aims to encourage scientific curiosity, improve research accessibility, and inspire students, educators, and space enthusiasts to explore the science of fire beyond Earth.
details: IGNIS (Intelligent Guidance & NASA Insights System) is an interactive scientific exploration platform designed to make combustion science and fire behaviour in microgravity accessible through research, data exploration, visualizations, comparisons, and AI-assisted scientific guidance. On Earth, gravity-driven buoyancy strongly influences flame shape, movement, and combustion. In microgravity, these effects are suppressed, allowing researchers to investigate combustion phenomena that are difficult to isolate under normal gravity. Understanding these differences is important for spacecraft fire-safety research, astronaut protection, and future human space exploration. IGNIS brings this research into one web-based platform through several integrated modules: • Research Explorer: A curated library of NASA-related combustion investigations and research records, including ACME, SoFIE, FLARE, FLEX, Saffire, SAME, SPICE, and the Combustion Integrated Rack. • Data Laboratory: A browser-based workspace that allows users to upload CSV files, validate and preview datasets, explore information, and export processed results. • Comparison Studio: Enables side-by-side comparison of up to four investigations using documented parameters, source information, data availability, and scientific limitations. • Visualization Studio: Presents interactive charts and visual explanations to help users explore combustion-related parameters and scientific concepts. • AI Research Assistant: Helps users investigate scientific questions, understand complex concepts, and navigate available research. It distinguishes general conversation from scientific queries and provides research-grounded responses where supporting information is available. • Space Fire Safety: Explores the relevance of combustion research to spacecraft safety and human spaceflight. • Methodology and Scientific Context: Communicates source provenance, data limitations, and the distinction between authentic research records and illustrative demonstration data. IGNIS was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, and Lucide icons. It is designed as a responsive web application that works across desktop and mobile devices, with local functionality available without requiring an account or external AI key. The project's creative approach is to combine scientific research discovery, comparative analysis, local data processing, interactive visualization, and conversational assistance into a single research-oriented experience. Instead of presenting isolated scientific facts, IGNIS helps users explore how different investigations relate to one another while respecting the limitations of the available evidence. The team considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, responsive design, usability, research provenance, data availability, and the importance of not presenting synthetic demonstration data as authentic NASA measurements. The intended impact is to make microgravity combustion research easier to discover and understand, encourage scientific curiosity, and improve awareness of the challenges associated with fire behaviour in spacecraft environments. IGNIS is an educational and research-exploration platform, not an operational fire-risk prediction or certification system.
